html:
Bijapur was a sultanate in the western Deccan of India, ruled by the Adil Shahi dynasty from about 1490 to 1686. Its founder, Yusuf Adil Shah, was a Bahmani governor who broke away as that state fell apart. It was one of the five Deccan sultanates.

  • It lost its port of Goa to the Portuguese in 1510 (Portuguese seize Goa).
  • It joined the alliance that defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota in 1565.
  • Ibrahim Adil Shah II, who ruled from 1580 to 1627, was a patron of music and painting and wrote songs himself.
  • It annexed Bidar in 1619.
  • The Gol Gumbaz, the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah, has one of the largest domes of its age.

In its last decades the Maratha leader Shivaji carved a kingdom out of its western lands. The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb took the city in 1686.
